description: USAGov’s benefit finder lets you explore government assistance by category and locate information about applying. It supplies starting points rather than a benefit approval.
introduction: USAGov’s benefit finder lets you explore government assistance by category and locate information about applying. It supplies starting points rather than a benefit approval.

who: Anyone researching assistance for themselves or their family can browse the finder. Eligibility is determined by the individual benefit program.
sections.get: Choose categories such as food, health, housing and utilities, disability, jobs, education or veterans to explore relevant benefits and application information.
sections.docs: Browsing categories is separate from submitting an application. Make a short list of the needs you want to address, then review each agency’s document instructions before applying.
sections.apply: Visit the USAGov benefit finder, select at least one category and choose Apply selections. Follow the resulting program information to the responsible agency.
sections.after: Compare the requirements of each promising program and note its application route. Keep applications and reference numbers separately so that one pending request is not confused with another.
sections.sources:
• USAGov benefit finder
  • USA Assistance background and screenshots

faqs: Does Apply selections submit a benefits application?
It applies your category choices to the search; the agency application is a separate step.
Yes. The finder allows multiple selections.
Can it help me research family benefits?
Yes. Children and families is one of its categories.
Does appearing in results mean I qualify?
No. Review the program requirements and seek the agency’s decision.

provenance.review_scope: Program purpose, eligibility pathway and application methods; no unverified dollar limits published.
